$comment: Written form -> spoken form, applied to narration before text-to-speech. Captions keep the written form. Matching is case-sensitive and whole-token, longest entry first. Prefer rewording a script over adding an entry; add one when a term must appear as written.

entries.note: Said or-LEENZ, stress on the second syllable. espeak-ng reads the written form as OR-lee-unz; the hyphenated respelling phonemizes to /O:l'i:nz/.
A lone capital A is read as the article (uh); 'Eh' phonemizes to the letter name /eI/.
As 'Cluster A': matching is case-sensitive, so each case needs its own entry.
espeak-ng mangles the written form; the hyphenated respelling is read as two familiar parts, idem and potent.

The verb, as in 'the store lives in the cluster': espeak-ng reads the written form as the plural of life (/laIvz/) in every context. The respelling phonemizes to /lIvz/. A script that needs the noun should say 'lifetimes', or add a phrase entry.
Scripts should say 'write-ahead log'; this is the fallback reading.
